paper_title: PyramidInfer Pyramid KV Cache Compression for High-throughput LLM   Inference
caption: The evaluation of inference methods using an A100 80GB GPU on LLaMA 2-13B and 70B. Length: prefill length + generation length. Bsz: batch size. KV mem.: GPU memory usage (GB) of the KV cache. Thr.: throughput (token/s) : S_r ratio ablation study.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the performance trade-offs of different inference methods as the “Recent Sequence Ratio (%)” varies from approximately 10% to 100% on an A100 80GB GPU, evaluated on LLaMA 2-13B and 70B models. The x-axis, labeled “Recent Sequence Ratio (%)”, spans from 10 to 100 in linear scale with tick marks every 20 units. The left y-axis, labeled “Perplexity”, ranges from 4.2 to 4.7 in linear scale with tick marks every 0.1 unit, and the right y-axis, labeled “GPU Mem. Ratio (%)”, ranges from 0 to 100 in linear scale with tick marks every 20 units. Four lines are plotted: “Perplexity” (orange solid line with circle markers) starts at ~4.6 at 10% ratio, drops sharply to ~4.3 at 40%, then fluctuates slightly before rising to ~4.4 at 100%; “Full Cache PPL” (red dashed line) remains constant at ~4.37 across all ratios; “GPU Mem. Ratio” (blue solid line with circle markers) increases gradually from ~40% at 10% ratio to ~95% at 100%; and “Full Cache GPU Mem.” (blue dashed line) remains constant at 100% across all ratios. The plot demonstrates how reducing the recent sequence ratio affects model perplexity and GPU memory utilization relative to full cache baselines.
